learn.hook: Can you find the exact middle of a line without measuring? A compass can do it — like a magic trick!
points: To bisect means to cut into two equal parts.
Perpendicular bisector of AB: with a compass opening MORE than half of AB, draw arcs from A and from B on both sides. Join the two points where the arcs cross.
The perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint of AB and makes a 90° angle with it.
Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is the same distance from A and from B.
Angle bisector: from the vertex draw an arc cutting both arms. From those two points draw arcs that cross. Join the vertex to the crossing point. It splits the angle into two equal halves.

example.q: Draw the perpendicular bisector of AB = 6 cm. Where does it cut AB?
steps: Open the compass to more than 3 cm (say 4 cm)
Draw arcs above and below AB from A, then from B with the same opening
Join the two crossing points; it cuts AB at its midpoint M
example.answer: At M, where AM = MB = 3 cm, at a right angle

learn.reallife: Builders find the middle of a wall, and gardeners mark paths that stay equally far from two trees, using the perpendicular bisector idea.

games.title: Perpendicular bisector steps
items: Draw the line segment AB
Open the compass to more than half of AB
With centre A, draw arcs above and below AB
With the same opening and centre B, draw arcs cutting the first two
Join the two crossing points

games.title: Bisector truths
items: The perpendicular bisector of AB meets AB at 90°.
That is why it is called perpendicular.
Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is equally far from A and B.
This is the special property of the perpendicular bisector.
For a perpendicular bisector, the compass opening can be less than half of AB.
Then the arcs from A and B would not meet.
An angle bisector splits an angle into two equal angles.
Bisect means cut into two equal parts.
Bisecting a 90° angle gives two 30° angles.
Half of 90° is 45°.
We need a protractor to draw a perpendicular bisector.
A ruler and a compass are enough.

quiz.q: AB = 8 cm. Its perpendicular bisector cuts AB at M. How long is AM?
quiz.explain: The perpendicular bisector cuts AB at its midpoint, so AM = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.
steps: M is the midpoint
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the bisector meets AB at the middle

quiz.q: What angle does the perpendicular bisector of AB make with AB?
quiz.explain: Perpendicular means it meets AB at a right angle, 90°.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'bisector' (half) with the angle it makes

quiz.q: To draw the perpendicular bisector of a 6 cm segment, what compass opening should you use?
quiz.explain: The opening must be more than half of 6 cm (3 cm), otherwise the arcs from the two ends will not meet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any small opening works

quiz.q: An angle of 80° is bisected. What is each new angle?
quiz.explain: Bisecting cuts the angle into two equal parts: 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the angle instead of halving it

quiz.q: P is a point on the perpendicular bisector of AB, and PA = 5 cm. What is PB?
quiz.explain: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is the same distance from A and B, so PB = PA = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Halves or doubles the distance

quiz.q: A 60° angle is bisected, and then one of the halves is bisected again. What is the smallest angle made?
quiz.mistake: Bisects only once

quiz.q: Which tools do you need to construct a perpendicular bisector?
options: A protractor and a set square
quiz.explain: The compass draws the arcs and the ruler joins the crossing points.
quiz.mistake: Thinks angles must be measured with a protractor

quiz.q: In an angle bisector construction, why are the two new angles equal?
options: The two triangles formed are congruent by SSS, so the matching angles are equal
quiz.explain: The arcs make two triangles with all three sides equal (SSS). Congruent triangles have equal matching angles.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the construction to congruent triangles

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find the exact middle of a stick drawn on paper, without a scale. How can he do it with a compass?
teach.praise: Wow! Two arcs from each end and one line — Gappu found the exact middle!
teach.nudge: How wide should the compass be, and what do you join at the end?

topics.title: Perpendiculars at a point, from outside, and with ropes

learn.hook: More than 2,500 years ago, builders in India made perfect right angles with just a knotted rope!
points: 90° at a point P on a line: with centre P, draw an arc cutting the line at A and B (so PA = PB). Then draw arcs from A and B with a bigger radius; they cross at Q. PQ is perpendicular to the line.
It works because Q is equally far from A and B, so PQ is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
Perpendicular from an outside point Q: with centre Q, draw an arc cutting the line at A and B. From A and B draw equal arcs crossing at R on the other side. QR is perpendicular to the line.
The Sulba-Sutras, ancient Indian texts for building fire altars, used ropes. A rope knotted into 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 equal parts, pulled into a triangle, gives a right angle.
Other rope triangles such as 5, 12, 13 also give right angles.

example.q: Draw a perpendicular to line l from a point Q outside it.
steps: With centre Q, draw an arc cutting l at A and B
With centres A and B and the same radius, draw arcs crossing at R on the other side of l
Join QR

learn.reallife: Masons still use a knotted string or a 3-4-5 check to make sure walls meet at a right angle.

games.title: Perpendicular at a point on a line
items: Mark point P on line l
With centre P, draw an arc cutting l at A and B
With a bigger radius, draw arcs from A and B that cross at Q
Join PQ — it is perpendicular to l

games.title: Ropes and arcs
items: A rope knotted into 3, 4 and 5 equal parts makes a right angle
3, 4, 5 is a right-triangle set.
The Sulba-Sutras were written for building fire altars
They give exact rules for altar shapes.
For a perpendicular from an outside point, the first arc is drawn with centre at that point
It cuts the line at two points.
A rope knotted into 2, 3 and 4 parts makes a right angle
2, 3, 4 does not give a right angle.
In the perpendicular-at-a-point method, PA must equal PB
P must be the midpoint of AB.

quiz.q: To construct a 90° angle at point P on a line, what is the first step?
options: Draw a line from P at any slant
With centre P, draw an arc cutting the line at two points A and B
quiz.explain: The arc makes PA = PB, so P becomes the midpoint of AB.
quiz.mistake: Reaches for a protractor instead of compass steps

quiz.q: In that construction, why is PQ perpendicular to the line?
options: Q is equally far from A and B, so PQ is the perpendicular bisector of AB
Because Q is above the line
quiz.explain: Points equidistant from A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB, which passes through the midpoint P.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason that does not use equal distances

quiz.q: To draw a perpendicular from a point Q outside a line, what is the first step?
options: With centre Q, draw an arc cutting the line at two points
Draw a line parallel to the given line
Draw a circle with centre on the line
quiz.explain: The two cutting points are equally far from Q; then we find another point equally far from them.
quiz.mistake: Starts the construction on the line instead of at Q

quiz.q: A rope is knotted into 12 equal parts to make a right angle. How are the parts shared among the three sides?
quiz.explain: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12, and a 3-4-5 triangle has a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Splits the rope equally, which gives 60° angles

quiz.q: In a 3-4-5 rope triangle, each part is 50 cm. How long is the longest side?
quiz.explain: 5 parts × 50 cm = 250 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the 4-part side

quiz.q: What were the Sulba-Sutras used for?
options: Building fire altars of exact shapes and sizes
quiz.explain: They gave geometric rules, including right angles made with ropes, for building altars.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the purpose of these ancient texts

quiz.q: Which other knotted-rope triangle also gives a right angle?
quiz.mistake: Picks lengths that just look close

quiz.q: How many equal parts are needed in total for a 5-12-13 rope triangle?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the sides

teach.ask: Gappu has no protractor, only a compass and a ruler. How can Gappu make a right angle at a point on a line?
teach.praise: Right angle made! Gappu's corner is perfect.
teach.nudge: What should Gappu draw first, with the compass point on P?

topics.title: Copying an angle and drawing parallel lines

learn.hook: Copy any angle exactly — no protractor, no measuring — just a compass and a ruler!
points: To copy ∠ABC at point Q on a ray: with centre B draw an arc cutting the arms at D and E.
With the same radius and centre Q, draw an arc cutting the ray at R.
Open the compass to the distance DE. With centre R, cut the second arc at S. Join QS: ∠SQR = ∠ABC.
It works because triangles DBE and SQR have three equal sides, so they are congruent (SSS).
To draw a parallel through P: draw a transversal through P cutting line l, then copy the angle at l to P in the corresponding position.

example.q: Draw a line through P parallel to l without a protractor.
steps: Draw a line through P cutting l at Q
Copy the angle at Q to P, in the corresponding position
The new line makes equal corresponding angles, so it is parallel to l
example.answer: A line through P parallel to l

learn.reallife: Tailors copy the angle of a collar from one shirt to another with just a measuring tape and a marker — the same idea.

games.title: Copying an angle
items: With centre B, draw an arc cutting the arms of ∠B at D and E
With the same radius and centre Q, draw an arc cutting the ray at R
Open the compass to the distance DE
With centre R, cut the second arc at S
Join QS

games.title: Copy check
items: Copying an angle needs a protractor
Only a compass and ruler are needed.
The copy works because of SSS congruence
The two triangles have three equal sides.
The first two arcs must have the same radius
That makes two pairs of equal sides.
To draw a parallel, copy the angle in the corresponding position
Equal corresponding angles mean parallel lines.
Copying an angle anywhere always gives a parallel line
It must be in the corresponding (or alternate) position.

quiz.q: Which tools are needed to copy an angle exactly?
options: A ruler and a compass only
quiz.explain: Arcs of equal radius and one copied distance are enough.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a protractor is always needed

quiz.q: What is the first step in copying ∠ABC?
options: With centre B, draw an arc cutting both arms
Draw a circle around the whole angle
quiz.explain: The arc from the vertex marks equal distances on both arms.
quiz.mistake: Starts at the wrong point

quiz.q: After the first arc, what is drawn at the new point Q?
options: An arc with centre Q and the same radius
An arc with centre Q and a bigger radius
quiz.explain: Using the same radius makes QR equal to BD.
quiz.mistake: Changes the compass opening

quiz.q: Which distance is copied with the compass in the third step?
options: The distance from B to Q
The distance DE between the points where the first arc cut the arms
quiz.explain: Copying DE gives the third pair of equal sides.
quiz.mistake: Copies an arm length instead

quiz.q: Why is the copied angle equal to the original?
options: The two triangles are congruent by SSS
quiz.explain: BD = QR, BE = QS and DE = RS, so the triangles are congruent and the matching angles are equal.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the construction to congruence

quiz.q: To draw a line through P parallel to l, which angle do we copy?
options: The angle between l and itself
The angle a transversal makes with l, placed at P in the corresponding position
quiz.explain: Equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel.
quiz.mistake: Copies the angle in the wrong position

quiz.q: A transversal makes 72° with l. What angle must be copied at P, in the corresponding position, for a parallel line?
quiz.explain: Corresponding angles must be equal: 72°.
quiz.mistake: Uses the linear-pair angle

quiz.q: Suppose you copy the 72° angle at P in the alternate position instead. Is the new line still parallel to l?
options: Yes — equal alternate angles also give parallel lines
quiz.explain: Equal alternate angles also show that two lines are parallel.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only one angle rule proves lines parallel

teach.ask: Gappu wants to copy a 50° angle but lost the protractor. Teach Gappu the compass trick!
teach.praise: Copied perfectly! Gappu's angle matches exactly.
teach.nudge: Which two distances must Gappu keep the same?

learn.hook: Step a compass around a circle using its own radius — it fits exactly 6 times and draws a perfect hexagon!
points: Eye design: two equal arcs join the same two points A and B, one curving up and one curving down. Each arc's centre lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB.

Pointed arch: with centres at the two ends of the span and radius equal to the span, draw arcs meeting at the top. The top and the two ends form an equilateral triangle. A trefoil arch fits three equal round lobes inside an arch.
Angles around a point add up to 360°.
Six equilateral triangles around a point (6 × 60° = 360°) make a regular hexagon; each of its angles is 60° + 60° = 120°.
A 6-pointed star: draw two overlapping equilateral triangles, or put an equilateral triangle on each side of a regular hexagon.

example.q: Construct a regular hexagon of side 3 cm.
steps: Draw a circle of radius 3 cm
Keeping the compass at 3 cm, step around the circle: it fits 6 times
Join the 6 points
example.answer: A regular hexagon with perimeter 18 cm

learn.reallife: Temple and mosque arches, jaali windows and rangoli stars across India are built from these compass designs.

items.q: Each angle of a regular hexagon
Equilateral triangles meeting at a hexagon's centre
Perimeter of a regular hexagon with side 3 cm
Missing angle: 120°, 90°, 60° and ? around a point

games.title: Design truths
items: Angles around a point add up to 360°
A full turn is 360°.
A regular hexagon can be made from 6 equilateral triangles
6 × 60° = 360° at the centre.
In a pointed arch, each arc's radius is half the span
The radius equals the whole span.
An eye design uses two equal arcs through the same two points
One curves up and one curves down.
A 6-pointed star can be made from two overlapping equilateral triangles
One points up and one points down.
Each angle of a regular hexagon is 60°
Each is 120°.
A trefoil arch has three rounded lobes
'Tri' means three and 'foil' means leaf: three equal lobes.

quiz.q: Four angles meet at a point: 150°, 90°, 70° and x. What is x?
quiz.explain: Angles around a point add to 360°: 360° − 150° − 90° − 70° = 50°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 180° instead of 360°

quiz.q: A regular hexagon is made of 6 equilateral triangles. What is each angle of the hexagon?
quiz.explain: At each corner of the hexagon, two triangle angles meet: 60° + 60° = 120°.
quiz.mistake: Takes just one triangle's angle

quiz.q: With the compass open to the circle's radius, how many steps fit around the circle?
quiz.explain: Each step makes an equilateral triangle with the centre, so 360° ÷ 60° = 6 steps.
quiz.mistake: Guesses 4 like the corners of a square

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a regular hexagon with side 5 cm?
quiz.explain: 6 equal sides: 6 × 5 = 30 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses 5 sides instead of 6

quiz.q: A pointed arch has a span of 6 m. What radius should each arc have?
quiz.explain: In a pointed arch, each arc's radius equals the span.
quiz.mistake: Uses half the span, which gives a round arch

quiz.q: In a pointed arch with span AB, the arc with centre A and the arc with centre B (both of radius AB) meet at the top point C. What kind of triangle is ABC?
options: Isosceles with AC = BC = half of AB
quiz.explain: AC is a radius of the arc centred at A, and BC is a radius of the arc centred at B. Both radii equal the span AB, so all three sides are equal.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that both arcs have radius equal to the span

quiz.q: In an eye design, two equal arcs pass through A and B. Where are the centres of the two arcs?
options: On the perpendicular bisector of AB
On the line AB, beyond A or B
quiz.explain: Each centre is equally far from A and B, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the centres are at the ends A and B

quiz.q: A 6-pointed star is drawn from two overlapping equilateral triangles. How many points does it have?
quiz.explain: Each triangle gives 3 points, and they don't overlap: 3 + 3 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts the points of only one triangle

teach.ask: Gappu wants to draw a rangoli hexagon with sides of 4 cm. What steps should Gappu follow?
teach.praise: Hexagon complete! Gappu's rangoli looks amazing.
teach.nudge: What radius should Gappu use, and how many times does it step around the circle?

learn.hook: No protractor? No problem! With only a compass you can make 60°, 30°, 90°, 45° and even 120°.
points: 60°: draw an arc from the vertex, then an arc of the SAME radius from where it cuts the arm. The three points form an equilateral triangle, so the angle is 60°.
120°: step the same arc twice along the first arc (60° + 60°).
30° = bisect 60°. 90° = construct a perpendicular. 45° = bisect 90°.
Square: all four sides equal and all angles 90°. Rectangle: opposite sides equal and all angles 90°.
Circle: open the compass to the radius, keep the point fixed and turn.

example.q: Construct an angle of 30° using only a ruler and a compass.
steps: Construct a 60° angle using arcs of the same radius
Bisect the 60° angle
Each half is 60° ÷ 2 = 30°

learn.reallife: Carpenters, tailors and rangoli artists use these exact angles to make neat, matching patterns.

quiz.q: How can you construct a 30° angle with a ruler and a compass?
quiz.explain: 60° ÷ 2 = 30°, so bisecting a constructed 60° angle gives 30°.
quiz.mistake: Bisects the wrong angle (90° ÷ 2 = 45°)

quiz.q: What angle do you get by bisecting a right angle?
quiz.explain: A right angle is 90°. Half of it is 45°.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the 60° construction with the 90° one

quiz.q: Riya constructs a 60° angle, then another 60° angle right next to it from the same vertex. What angle do the outer arms make?
quiz.mistake: Thinks the angle stays 60°

quiz.q: To construct a square ABCD with side 4 cm, Arjun draws AB = 4 cm. What should he do next?
options: Make a 90° angle at A and mark AD = 4 cm
quiz.explain: A square has right angles and equal sides, so the next side starts at 90° from AB and is also 4 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that all angles of a square are 90°

quiz.q: Kabir draws a circle with his compass opened to 3 cm. What is the diameter of the circle?
quiz.explain: The compass opening is the radius (3 cm). Diameter = 2 × radius = 6 cm.
steps: Radius = 3 cm
Diameter = 2 × 3 = 6 cm
quiz.mistake: Gives the radius instead of the diameter

quiz.q: Which two constructed angles, placed side by side, make 135°?
quiz.explain: 90° + 45° = 135°. Both can be made with a compass.
quiz.mistake: Adds the wrong pair of angles

quiz.q: Aisha constructs a rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Perimeter = 2 × (5 + 3) = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the area (15) or adds only two sides (8)

quiz.q: In the 60° construction, why is the angle exactly 60°?
options: The vertex and the two arc points form an equilateral triangle, whose angles are all 60°
quiz.explain: All three distances are the same compass radius, so the triangle is equilateral and each angle is 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the hidden equilateral triangle

teach.ask: Gappu has only a ruler and a compass. How can he make a 30° angle?
teach.praise: Hooray! Make 60° with equal arcs, then cut it in half. Gappu made 30°!
teach.nudge: Which angle do you make first, and what do you do to it?

learn.hook: Why are bathroom tiles squares and beehive cells hexagons — but never pentagons? Let's crack the tiling code!
points: A tiling covers a flat surface with shapes that leave no gaps and do not overlap.
At every point where corners meet, the angles must add up to 360°.
Only three regular polygons tile on their own: equilateral triangles (6 × 60°), squares (4 × 90°) and regular hexagons (3 × 120°).
A regular pentagon has 108° angles. 360 ÷ 108 is not a whole number, so pentagons leave gaps.
Different shapes can tile together: two regular octagons (135° each) and one square (90°) fit around a point.

example.q: Can regular pentagons tile a floor on their own?
steps: Each angle of a regular pentagon is 108°
No whole number of pentagons makes exactly 360°

learn.reallife: Floor tiles, brick walls, honeycombs and rangoli borders are all tilings. Some old Indian palaces have amazing tiled floors and windows!

games.title: Tiles on its own?
items: Equilateral triangle
Square
Regular hexagon
Rectangle
Regular pentagon
Regular octagon
Circle

games.title: Tiling truths
items: In a tiling, tiles may overlap each other.
A tiling has no gaps and no overlaps.
The angles meeting at a point in a tiling add up to 360°.
They go all the way around the point.
Regular hexagons can tile a floor.
Regular pentagons can tile a floor on their own.
108° does not fit into 360° a whole number of times.
Six equilateral triangles fit around one point.
Circles can tile a floor without gaps.
Circles always leave curved gaps between them.

quiz.q: In a floor of square tiles, how many squares meet at each corner point?
quiz.explain: Each square corner is 90°. 360° ÷ 90° = 4 squares.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the angles must make a full 360°

quiz.q: How many equilateral triangles meet at a point in a triangle tiling?
quiz.explain: Each angle is 60°. 360° ÷ 60° = 6 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3 triangles meet because a triangle has 3 corners

quiz.q: Each angle of a regular hexagon is 120°. How many hexagons meet at a point in a honeycomb tiling?
quiz.explain: 360° ÷ 120° = 3 hexagons.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 6 meet because a hexagon has 6 sides

quiz.q: Why can't regular pentagons tile a floor on their own?
options: Their 108° angles do not fit into 360° a whole number of times
Pentagons have an odd number of sides
quiz.explain: 3 pentagons make 324° (gap) and 4 make 432° (overlap). No whole number gives exactly 360°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks having an odd number of sides is the reason

quiz.q: Regular octagons (135° each) and squares tile together. At each point, 2 octagons meet. How many squares are needed there?
quiz.explain: 2 × 135° = 270°. 360° − 270° = 90°, which is exactly one square corner.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract the octagon angles from 360°

quiz.q: At a point in a tiling, the angles are 90°, 60°, 60° and x. What is x?
quiz.explain: All angles around the point add up to 360°. x = 360° − 90° − 60° − 60° = 150°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 180° instead of 360°

quiz.q: Which shape can NOT tile a floor on its own?
quiz.explain: A regular octagon has 135° angles. 2 × 135° = 270° and 3 × 135° = 405°, so octagons alone leave gaps.
quiz.mistake: Thinks shapes with more sides fit together better

quiz.q: Meena's room floor is 3 m by 2 m. She uses square tiles of side 50 cm. How many tiles does she need?
quiz.explain: Along 3 m: 300 ÷ 50 = 6 tiles. Along 2 m: 200 ÷ 50 = 4 tiles. Total = 6 × 4 = 24 tiles.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change metres into centimetres

teach.ask: Gappu wants to tile his nest floor. What rules must the tiles follow, and why do hexagons work?
teach.praise: Ahaa! No gaps, no overlaps, and the corners make 360°. Gappu's nest looks like a honeycomb now!
teach.nudge: What must the angles at a meeting point add up to?

topics.title: Tangrams, dominoes and the chessboard trick

learn.hook: Remove two opposite corners from a chessboard. Can 31 dominoes cover the rest? Colours give a surprising answer!
points: A tangram is a square cut into 7 pieces: 2 large triangles, 1 medium triangle, 2 small triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram.
If the whole square has area 16 units, each large triangle is 4, the medium triangle 2, each small triangle 1, the square 2 and the parallelogram 2.
A 2 × 1 domino always covers 2 squares, so a region with an odd number of squares (like 5 × 5 = 25) can never be tiled by dominoes.
Colouring argument: on a chessboard each domino covers one black and one white square.
Removing two opposite corners (both the same colour) leaves 32 squares of one colour and 30 of the other, so no domino tiling exists — even though 62 is even.

example.q: Can a 3 × 5 grid be tiled by 2 × 1 dominoes?
steps: 3 × 5 = 15 squares
Each domino covers 2 squares
15 is odd, so some square is always left over

learn.reallife: Puzzle lovers have played with tangrams for centuries, and engineers use colouring arguments to prove when designs are impossible.

games.title: Domino tiling possible?
items: 2 × 3 grid
3 × 3 grid
4 × 5 grid
5 × 5 grid
8 × 8 board
8 × 8 board with two opposite corners removed
1 × 7 strip
2 × 7 strip

games.title: Tangram and domino truths
items: A tangram has 7 pieces
5 triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram.
The tangram square piece is bigger than a large triangle
The square is 2 units; a large triangle is 4.
Any region with an even number of squares can be tiled by dominoes
The cut chessboard has 62 squares but cannot be tiled.
Each domino on a chessboard covers one black and one white square
Neighbouring squares have different colours.
A 3 × 5 grid can be covered by dominoes
15 squares is odd.

quiz.q: How many pieces does a tangram have?
quiz.explain: 2 large, 1 medium and 2 small triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram: 7 pieces.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the square or the parallelogram

quiz.q: How many of the tangram pieces are triangles?
quiz.explain: 2 large + 1 medium + 2 small = 5 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the large triangles

quiz.q: The whole tangram square has area 16 units. What is the area of one large triangle?
quiz.explain: Each large triangle is a quarter of the whole square: 16 ÷ 4 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a large triangle is half the square

quiz.q: The whole tangram square has area 16 units. What is the area of the small square piece?
quiz.explain: The square piece is made of two small triangles (1 unit each): 2 units.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the square is the biggest piece

quiz.q: Can a 5 × 5 grid be tiled exactly by 2 × 1 dominoes?
options: Yes, if we turn some dominoes
No — 25 squares is odd, but each domino covers 2
quiz.explain: 12 dominoes cover 24 squares, leaving 1 square; 13 would need 26 squares.
quiz.mistake: Ignores whether the total is odd or even

quiz.q: How many 2 × 1 dominoes are needed to tile a 4 × 6 grid?
quiz.explain: 4 × 6 = 24 squares, and each domino covers 2: 24 ÷ 2 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of squares

quiz.q: Two opposite corners are removed from an 8 × 8 chessboard. How many squares are left?
quiz.explain: 64 − 2 = 62 squares.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract the removed corners

quiz.q: Why can't 31 dominoes cover the chessboard with two opposite corners removed?
options: Dominoes cannot be placed near corners
Both removed squares are the same colour, leaving 32 of one colour and 30 of the other
quiz.explain: Each domino covers one black and one white square, so we would need equal numbers of each colour.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every even-sized region can be tiled

teach.ask: Gappu wants to cover a 3 × 3 board with dominoes. Can Gappu do it? Explain why.
teach.praise: Exactly! 9 squares can't be split into pairs.

learn.hook: In 2023 a shape called the 'hat' was discovered — it covers a floor forever but NEVER repeats its pattern!
points: The Dutch artist M. C. Escher made tilings of interlocking birds, fish and lizards.
Trick: cut a piece from one side of a square tile and stick it on the opposite side — the new wiggly tile still tiles.
In 2023 a 13-sided shape called the 'hat' was found that tiles a flat surface but never in a repeating pattern.
Honeybees build hexagonal cells. Hexagons fit together with no gaps and use less wax for the space they hold than squares or triangles.
Wasp nests also have hexagonal cells — nature loves hexagons!

example.q: How can you make an Escher-style tile from a square?
steps: Cut a shape out of the left side of a square
Slide it across and stick it on the right side
Do the same for the top and bottom if you like
The new tile still fits together with no gaps
example.answer: Cut from one side and add to the opposite side

learn.reallife: Look closely at a honeycomb, a football's patches or the floor tiles at a railway station — tilings are everywhere.

quiz.q: Which artist is famous for tilings made of interlocking birds, fish and lizards?
quiz.explain: M. C. Escher, a Dutch artist, created many such tilings.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous artists

quiz.q: What shape are the cells in a honeycomb?
quiz.explain: Bees build six-sided (hexagonal) cells.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cells are round

quiz.q: Why are hexagons a good shape for bees?
options: They fit with no gaps and use less wax for the space they hold
They are the easiest shape to count
They have the most corners of any shape
They are always the same colour
quiz.explain: Hexagons tile without gaps and need less wall material than squares or triangles holding the same space.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason that has nothing to do with gaps or wax

quiz.q: What was special about the 'hat' tile discovered in 2023?
options: It tiles a floor but never in a repeating pattern
quiz.explain: It is the first known single shape that can only tile without ever repeating.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every tiling must repeat

quiz.q: How many sides does the 'hat' tile have?
quiz.explain: The hat is a 13-sided shape.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a common polygon

quiz.q: How can you make an Escher-style tile from a square?
options: Cut a piece from one side and stick it on the opposite side
quiz.explain: The bump on one side matches the dent on the next tile, so there are still no gaps.
quiz.mistake: Removes pieces without adding them back

quiz.q: In the middle of a honeycomb, how many neighbouring cells does each hexagonal cell touch?
quiz.explain: Each of its 6 sides is shared with one neighbouring cell.
quiz.mistake: Counts the cells meeting at one corner instead

quiz.q: What shape are the cells of a paper wasp's nest?
quiz.explain: Wasps also build hexagonal cells that fit together without gaps.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only bees use hexagons
